scope: Synthetic-only evaluation of a normalized fixed-proposal importance-particle approximation to the same conditional law, with exact integration of focal LC choices. No real cache, likelihood queries, fitting or native simulation.
basis: The original160000 references are current-head eligible, but30027 require5-10 random actors and overflow cap4. Even the shared in-domain symbolic bound is1.303B full forwards. Exact cached derivatives do not solve first-enumeration scaling.

fixed.population_law: Keep the existing current-geometry selector, full responsive background, canonical current-goal features, priors, residual nodes, permissions, LC order and observation kernel. No participant pruning or physical-rule changes.
fixed.new_cap5_case: Five ordinary lanes a0..a4 on road a, length200, no connections, same frozen vehicle/road fixture defaults. Insert right(a1,44,5), left(a3,45,5), outer(a4,52,5), farleft(a0,46,5), focal(a2,40,5), in that order. Focal is last. Require the unchanged selector to return exactly5 actors before responses.
fixed.new_cap10_case: Same road. Insert side actors at a0 positions30,38,46; a1 positions32,40; a3 positions30,38; a4 positions32,40, all speed5; focal is last at a2,40,speed5. No other actor occupies the focal longitudinal lane. Require exactly10 selected actors before responses.
parameter_probes: One deterministic nonzero point: theta[b,j]=0.1*(-1)^(b+j)/(j+1), using the existing fixed block order b=0..4 and canonical feature index j=0..p-1.
fixed.proposal: q0 is the frozen zero-coefficient law. Draw all selected current intents/residual/permission nodes, receiving intents and the LC prefix before focal; outside J use exactly the declared fixed intervention.
fixed.reuse: One1024-particle pool per case/replicate; the first256 form the paired smaller estimate. Both theta points and finite differences reuse the same particles, features and masks. No seed replacement or parameter search.

estimator: Sample full physical latent choices and resolve the whole synthetic frame once per particle. For LC sample only the prefix before the focal actor. Integrate the focal masked3-class softmax exactly and integrate the LC suffix to1. Keep every participant in physical resolution.
For a focal that ends, omit its LC variable and integrate unneeded LC variables to1. Retain its END outcome in the common mixture.

All heads share the same prefix importance weights w(theta)=p_theta(sampled latent prefix)/q0(prefix). Do not combine physical-only Rao-Blackwell motion estimates with prefix-weighted LC estimates in the same reported joint law.

Normalize the common empirical mixture by sum_i w_i(theta). Motion/start/LC use the same survival denominator sum_i w_i D_i; entry uses sum_i w_i. Joint(class,speed) includes the exact focal-class factor and sums over classes to the same motion estimate.

Differentiate the finite normalized estimator itself, including both the shared importance-weight score and focal softmax derivatives. Entry must include the derivative of sum_i w_i even though the population normalizer is1. Use log-domain accumulation and no probability floor.
Call the result a finite-particle SNIS approximation with possible NLL/gradient bias, not the exact population likelihood or gradient.
reference: Retain exact cached and independent-enumeration references at both frozen theta points for all original13 cases and the fixed5-actor case. A synthetic computational cap extension here does not extend real-data admission.

For cap10, the focal motion is independent of side-actor physical residuals on this ordinary interior lane. Enumerate the2^10 longitudinal draws without LC to verify this property before sampling. Use the two focal speeds mu0 and mu1 from the frozen physical proposal and the known focal brake probability for a closed-form motion likelihood and190-vector gradient. Do not claim a cap10 LC oracle.

Use the previous frozen observation queries: motion at0,.05,.1,1; eligible start/entry labels0/1; eligible LC classes0/1/2; joint(class,speed) at speeds0/1. Compare only quantities with an exact/closed oracle; report known structural zeros separately.
checks: At both theta points, each finite common mixture normalizes, END plus survival mass is1, applicable event probabilities sum1, and joint class-speed sums to the same motion head; tolerance1e-10.

At1024 particles in the first fixed replicate of each case, check finite-SNIS analytic NLL gradients against central differences at both theta points, using the original five block directions plus mixed nonbias direction, h1e-5 and absolute1e-7+relative1e-5 tolerance. Do not resample for differences.
After particle construction, use failing physical-resolution stubs during all theta reuse and differences. Report physical preparation separately from particle-resolution counts.

Across all32 replicates and both particle budgets, report NLL/gradient bias, RMSE and95th absolute error against each available oracle, plus zero-numerator/zero-survival rates. ESS and maximum normalized weight explain failures but do not replace oracle errors.

For oracle-positive queries with zero sample numerator or denominator, preserve the failed replicate and infinite NLL/undefined gradient. Do not floor, drop it, select another seed, or extend the particle budget. Include these failures in the overall decision, rather than summarizing only finite survivors.
decision: Separate implementation consistency from finite-budget statistical error. Any consistency failure or oracle-positive zero-support failure at1024 makes this proposal unready for real fitting. Otherwise judge measured bias/noise and convergence at the frozen budgets; a synthetic pass never admits arbitrary theta, all5-10-actor LC distributions, or the complete160000 target.
after: Stop after this fixed synthetic comparison or a technical HOLD. No automatic real-data sampling/cache construction or fitting; a later real-data design needs its own cost and estimation budget.
storage: Process one synthetic case/replicate at a time, reuse its particles across theta/readouts, and persist compact metrics and failed-seed references rather than all particle trajectories. No server dataset download is needed.
